media.title: Paris, Eiffel Tower from the Trocadéro — migration context image
media.description: One half of a stereograph card showing the Eiffel Tower and the Champ de Mars from the Trocadéro, used as broad Paris context for Kaper’s 1933–34 period.
media.altText: Half of a stereograph card: the Eiffel Tower and Champ de Mars seen past a bronze eagle on the Trocadéro terrace.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The card prints its own number and title, “3190 Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower from the Trocadero Palace, Paris, France”, and the Library of Congress catalogues it under LCCN 2004674653 as a Keystone View Company stereograph of about 1931, noting “Copyright by the Keystone View Co., No. 3190; no copyright renewal” and advising no known restrictions on publication. Keystone published in the United States, so the URAA, which restored copyright only in foreign works, does not reach it; and a United States work first published in 1931 whose copyright was not renewed in its twenty-eighth year entered the public domain at the end of 1959. The Library of Congress marks this record as carrying unverified old data from the caption card, which is the source of both the date and the copyright note.
